name: README — import + ISA-101 + Tier0-Edge adaptation
info:
## TinyRL UNS alarm dashboard (ISA-101 style) - import notes

**Requires**: palette `node-red-dashboard` (Menu -> Manage palette -> Install) + built-in MQTT nodes. No other palettes.

**Import**: Menu -> Import -> select file -> Deploy. Dashboard: `http://<node-red-host>:1880/ui`
Theme note: keep the dashboard theme light/grey (Dashboard -> Theme) to match the ISA-101 baseline.

**ISA-101 design rules applied**
- Greyscale baseline: healthy states (IDLE / LEARNING / OK) are GREY; colour is reserved for abnormal
- RED = alarm OR a labeled FAULT condition (the State/condition kind); YELLOW = attention/diagnostic (unlabeled 'unknown' open ask)
- Banner line 1: <id> <CONDITION> [FAULT|NORMAL chip] (STATE) - the condition name is the large element
- Command buttons are neutral; only LABEL is yellow (it answers an attention state)
- Level-1 display: state banner + confidence trend + event list + command row
- Detail data (fw, features, lib_max, node identity) intentionally left to Tier0

**Broker**: default `192.168.201.99:1883` (site default) - edit the "UNS broker - EDIT ME" config node.
**Tier0-Edge**: point at your UNS broker (default `mqtt.tier0.dev:1883`) with the credentials
generated on the Edge tab. Inside Tier0's built-in Node-RED, delete this broker config and
re-select the UNS broker on each mqtt node (Tier0 binds the embedded broker by flow name).

**Layout**: three columns - Machine (both nodes in one ISA-101 table;
the OPEN ASK badge carries the ask's batch id), Events (one shared log
with a batch column), Label & control. All pipelines live on this one
sheet; each message's node is derived from its topic.

**Topics** (g100 UNS_BASE = `v1/Plant01/Motor-Test-Area/Line1/Power-Node-01`)
- subscribe: `State/condition`, `State/event`, `State/keepalive`, `Action/feedback` (parsed JSON);
  keepalive beats every 10 s, the status chip flips OFFLINE (red) after 30 s of silence
  State/condition carries kind=normal|fault when condition_id names a labeled library entry
- publish: `Action/feedback`, QoS 1, retain=false:
  `{"action":"start"}` | `{"action":"normal"}` | `{"action":"fault"}` |
  `{"action":"discard","batch":"P0001"}` | `{"action":"label","label":"<slug>","by":"human|agent|console"}`

**meas key vocabulary** (from `uns/uns.json`): g100 fset [Hz], v [V], i [A], pf [];
vib rms [g], b2 [g2], rms_y [g], centroid [Hz].

**Ask flow**: `State/condition` carries `batch` while an ask is live - the
Machine table shows it, and LABEL/DISCARD answer that id.

**Controls**: pick the node, then LABEL answers its ask (label slug + optional batch id +
kind normal/fault; kind defaults to fault, empty batch = the live episode), DISCARD deletes
the stored batch (model untouched), START/NORMAL/FAULT send bare verbs, RESET factory-wipes
the node - press once to arm, again within 10 s to confirm. Every command publishes
`{"action":...}` JSON to the selected node's `Action/feedback` - the node parses JSON;
a bare string parses to all-empty fields.

**Cadence note**: `State/condition` is change-driven + retained (quiet = healthy), so the
"last update [s]" counter is informational only - it ticks via a 5 s heartbeat inject and
does NOT raise a stale alarm.

**SIM injects**: editor-only, for offline testing - ignore in production.

name: AI assistant — Z.ai GLM chat (env: ZAI_API_KEY, ZAI_MODEL)
info:
## AI assistant (chat over your UNS data)

**Usage**: type in the ask box, press SEND. The assistant also wakes itself on every new alarm episode.

**Inference**: Z.ai OpenAI-compatible endpoint (https://api.z.ai/api/paas/v4/chat/completions), model defaults to glm-5.3-flash (override with ZAI_MODEL). The model runs forced thinking (docs.z.ai: GLM-5.3-Flash cannot disable it; depth = reasoning_effort low|high|max, server default max). The flow pins reasoning_effort=low (ZAI_REASONING env overrides) and max_tokens 1024 - thinking shares the budget, and max-effort reasoning caused the gateway timeouts and empty replies. Transient failures retry up to 3 attempts silently; a watch analysis that still fails stays silent (the alarm is on the banner), a manual question shows one error row. The assistant is read-only on watch triggers: labeling happens only when the operator names the condition and kind in the ask box. The prompt is intentionally minimal. Requests are serialized (one in flight; manual questions jump the queue; watch analyses take one queue slot and the newest replaces older pending ones).

**Context sent to the model**: live machine status (flow: cond_*, ka_*), last 10 events (flow: eventRows), last 8 chat turns (flow: ai_history).

**Setup**: add ZAI_API_KEY (and optional ZAI_MODEL) to the screenflow service env in docker-compose.override.yml with the values in deploy/.env, then:
bash bin/compose.sh up -d screenflow

**Auto watch**: ai_fn_watch taps the State/condition inputs; dedup key is node|condition_id|batch|ts_ms, plus a 60 s per-node cooldown. Auto analyses show as yellow "watch" bubbles.

**Write access**: the assistant answers asks itself (skills.md Skill 2). A trailing {"ai_action":{...}} block in its reply is validated then published to Action/feedback with by=agent: label (prefer by batch id; kind defaults to fault), discard, normal, fault. reset and start are refused - human-only (skills.md non-negotiables). Sends AND refusals are logged in the chat as the audit trail (green AI-write / red bubbles).
